key_insight: AutoDrude learns polarizable Drude force fields directly from DFT data and captures polymer-electrolyte ion transport more faithfully than fixed-charge or charge-scaled models.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster molecular dynamics simulations of solid polymer electrolytes with near-experimental conductivity and better prediction of cation transport behavior.
method: Differentiable end-to-end parametrization of Drude force fields from DFT energies, forces, and dipoles
Hard-constraint and soft-constraint variants for matching target dipoles
Benchmarked on PEO-LiTFSI against fixed-charge and charge-scaled baselines
evidence_signal: For PEO-LiTFSI, the hard-constraint model matches experimental ionic conductivity with 17% mean absolute percentage error, comparable to the best charge-scaled model at 16%, while also reproducing transference number trends and low-concentration ion pairing behavior.
watch_item: The soft-constraint variant fits DFT data more closely but can underestimate conductivity by up to an order of magnitude, so lower training error does not guarantee correct transport predictions.
paper_title: Drude, Where's My Charge? End-to-End Learning of Polarizable Drude Force Fields for Polymer Electrolytes
